enthrall

en-THRAWL · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To enthrall is to fully hold the attention of, through fascination or wonder.

The storyteller's account of the shipwreck enthralled every child in the room.

Worked Example

The chess grandmaster's endgame enthralled onlookers who had never before cared about chess.

Enthrall describes total captivation through fascination or awe -- audiences can't look away.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

captivate: To captivate is to attract and hold someone's interest -- a charming speaker captivates a crowd, and the crowd happily stays to listen. Enthrall grips harder: an enthralled audience is held as if by a spell, unable to look away even if they meant to. Captivated listeners enjoy staying; enthralled ones cannot look away.

mesmerize: To mesmerize is to hold someone's attention so completely that they freeze and stare -- the word comes from Mesmer, an early hypnotist, and it keeps that spellbound stillness. Enthrall holds attention just as tightly but through fascination and wonder at the thing itself: an enthralled audience is full of awe, not blank.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

bore: make weary through dullness

repel: cause strong dislike in

Where it sits · how tightly it grips the attention — interest → enthrall → hypnotize

interest vs. enthrall: Interesting someone is mild; enthralling them means they truly cannot look away.

hypnotize vs. enthrall: To hypnotize someone is to take over their will entirely, a step beyond simply enthralling their attention.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — en-

prefix — en-: to put into a state of (Old English/Old Norse)

root — thrall

root — thrall: a slave, a state of servitude (Old Norse (þræll))

Put it together

Put it together: en- ("to put into a state of") + thrall ("servitude") = to put into a spellbound state, as if enslaved by fascination.

Use the root in a new word: thralldom

Use the root in a new word: thralldom: The archaic noun "thralldom" once described the literal state of being enslaved -- the same root enthrall still echoes today.
